summary: Godot reports a broken resource reference only when that scene loads, and a dead signal connection never at all. godot-refcheck reads the project files instead: missing paths, case-only breakage, uid problems, connections to nodes that are gone. It repairs the ones with a single provable answer.
key_features: Ten checks over .tscn, .tres, project.godot, .import, plugin.cfg, GDScript and shaders, in both the Godot 3 and Godot 4 formats
Node paths resolve through instanced, inherited and placeholder scenes, so a dead signal connection is found without ever calling a healthy one broken
--fix repairs in place what the project itself settles: a moved file, a case-only difference, a uid that already resolves; two files with the same name produce no repair
Verified against a headless Godot: eight engine-confirmed cases and two repair round trips where the engine errors before --fix and is silent after
Calibrated on 237 projects in eleven real repositories: 41 findings, each confirmed by hand, no change proposed anywhere

social.headline: Godot only tells you a reference is broken when that scene loads. godot-refcheck tells you at commit time.

provenance.rule: mechanical fields read from the repository; counts taken from a run recorded in CI; no field is generated from a guess
